All main readings largely agree.

## Within Judaism
The line expresses a general assurance rather than a dated claim. Its purpose is comfort. Held by Jewish readers.

## Within Christianity
The line expresses personal conviction rather than a prediction. Its purpose is encouragement. Held by Christian readers.

## Where they agree
Both readings express confidence.

## Where they part, and why
The traditions differ over context rather than the central assurance.

## What the text settles
Its grammar gives a statement rather than a command, without specifying an occasion.

## Questions to take back to the text
1. How does the wider context develop the assurance?
2. What did you bring to the line before reading it?
